description_full: The Trade Desk, Inc. operates as a technology company in the United States and internationally. The company creates, manages, and optimizes digital advertising campaigns across ad formats, channels and devices, including CTV and other video, display, audio, and native, on a multitude of devices, such televisions, streaming devices, mobile devices, computers and digital-out-of-home devices. It provides data and other value-added services. It serves advertising agencies, advertisers, and other service providers for agencies or advertisers. The Trade Desk, Inc. was incorporated in 2009 and is headquartered in Ventura, California.

financial_summary: The Trade Desk, Inc. is a mid-cap communication services business with a $6.1B market cap on $2.9B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +22% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 26% against a 11% cost of capital — a 15-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $796M in free cash flow — roughly 27 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.24× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -8.9% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 22.6% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and stock-based comp at 17% of revenue is silent dilution an owner has to account for, and insiders hold 2.6% of the shares.

hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $1.3B (21% of market cap).
growth: Revenue has compounded at 22.4% over 3 years and 28.2% over 5 years, so growth is decelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 12%).

Capex runs 1.7x depreciation (6.8% of sales), so it is building capacity for future growth.
